newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai govt helps ailing property sector.
newsitem.headline: Thai govt helps ailing property sector.

text.p: Thai central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Tuesday the government had stepped in to rescue the property market from the effects of a prolonged property slump which has created a big supply glut.
He told reporters the three-year slump had left an oversupply of 350,000 housing and condominium units in Bangkok and its satellite towns at end-1996.

The governor said the glut in the residential sector grew last year despite a slower increase in newly-built houses which reached only 70,000 units in 1996 against previous annual average growth of 130,000 units.
The Thai cabinet earlier on Tuesday endorsed a 70 billion baht ($2.8 billion) property sector rescue package.

Deputy Finance Minister Chavarat Chanvirakul said the package included a plan for the state-owned Government Savings Bank and the Government Housing Bank to loan up to 20 billion baht of concessional mortgages to civil servants buying their first homes.
Under the scheme, civil servants will be charged an eight to nine percent mortgage rate against 13-14 percent carried by normal commercial bank loans.
Another 50 billion baht contributed by the government and commercial banks would be used for temporary takeovers of private property projects facing short-term financing problems.
